title: The power line that could reshape New York’s grid is hitting snags
gist: The $6 billion, 339-mile Champlain Hudson Power Express — North America's longest underground transmission line, built by Blackstone-owned Transmission Developers with Hydro-Québec and opened in May — could supply up to 20% of New York City's electricity, but has been down for most of July after two outages traced to a damaged cable on the US side. NYISO explicitly did not assume CHPE availability in its summer planning, and three years of Quebec drought are eroding the hydropower reserves that feed the line.

insights.claim: The Champlain Hudson Power Express is a 339-mile buried line running from Quebec to Queens, officially the longest underground transmission line in North America, and it opened in May.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Establishes the reference asset for underground HVDC economics — every subsequent buried interconnector will be benchmarked to its cost and reliability record.
insights.locator: Some of that power shuttled in on a 339-mile power line

insights.claim: CHPE was privately funded at a total cost of $6 billion by Transmission Developers, a company owned by alternative asset manager Blackstone, in partnership with Hydro-Québec.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A fully private $6bn merchant transmission build is the template alternative-asset managers will point to for infrastructure fund deployment into grid interconnection.
insights.locator: Transmission Developers, a company owned by the alternative asset management firm Blackstone

insights.claim: The CHPE permitting process formally began in March 2010 and construction did not start until late 2022, meaning roughly 15 years elapsed from planning to an operating line.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A 15-year lead time is the real discount rate problem in transmission investing — it caps how fast interconnection can respond to load growth.
insights.locator: Planning for the CHPE (which is charmingly pronounced “chippy”) started 15 years ago

insights.claim: CHPE consists of a bundle of two high-voltage direct-current cables each roughly five inches across, buried underground or under water, much of it trenched into Hudson River sediment by boats using water jets.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Underwater/underground burial is what made the permitting possible but also creates the repair-access problem now visible in the outage record.
insights.locator: The construction of this line was a feat

insights.claim: On July 3, during a heat wave, New York State's grid imported 52 gigawatt-hours of electricity from Canada — about 9% of its total electricity demand that day.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Quantifies existing cross-border dependence during peak stress — a metric to watch as a tariff/trade-policy exposure for the Northeast grid.
insights.locator: On July 3, as a heat wave swept the region

insights.claim: CHPE could supply up to 20% of New York City's electricity demand, largely with Quebec hydropower, in a state that still relies on fossil fuels for most of its generation.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A single asset carrying a fifth of NYC load is a material displacement of in-city gas generation — watch downstate fossil plant economics and capacity prices.
insights.locator: It could provide up to 20% of New York City's electricity demand

insights.claim: Over 99% of Quebec's electricity comes from renewable sources, mostly hydropower, with wind capacity growing quickly — the reason importing from Quebec is an emissions play, not just a supply play.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: The carbon-intensity differential is what makes the interconnection valuable for state clean-energy mandates, which underwrites the contracted revenue.
insights.locator: Over 99% of Quebec's electricity comes from renewable sources

insights.claim: Interconnection between grids both cuts emissions and lowers system costs by moving power to where it is needed, limiting how much new generating capacity has to be built.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Transmission substitutes for generation capex — the mental model for why transmission is the higher-leverage decarbonisation investment.
insights.locator: Connecting grids together can help accelerate the transition

insights.claim: CHPE has suffered two outages since opening: one on July 1 reportedly caused by a converter trip on the Canadian side, and a second beginning July 4 that had the line still down as of the morning of July 22.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Nearly three weeks of unplanned downtime in the first operating summer is a direct hit to merchant transmission revenue assumptions.
insights.locator: But CHPE is off to a slow start and has seen two outages so far

insights.claim: The second outage was traced to a damaged section of cable on the US side of the border, which has been removed and replaced, with Hydro-Québec's spokesperson estimating remaining work and post-repair testing would finish by the weekend.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A localised cable fault rather than a systemic design flaw is the bullish read — but it also shows repair cycles on buried cable run to weeks, not hours.
insights.quote: It is currently estimated that the remaining work, including necessary post-repair testing, will be completed by the weekend.
insights.locator: The damaged portion of the cable has been removed and replaced

insights.claim: Physicist Normand Mousseau of Université de Montréal argues such startup problems are not unusual because the equipment is not really fully tested until it is in operation, a view echoed by the pattern at other new power lines.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: If commissioning faults are structural to the asset class, first-year availability haircuts should be standard in transmission underwriting.
insights.locator: Some experts say this isn't unusual for a new infrastructure project

insights.claim: The 145-mile New England Clean Energy Connect line from Quebec to Maine, which opened in January, has also seen outages and delivered very little additional energy into the Northeast — making CHPE the second Quebec interconnector in a row to underdeliver at startup.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Two-for-two underperformance on Quebec export lines undercuts the assumption that Canadian hydro imports can be counted on for Northeast decarbonisation this decade.
insights.locator: Similar woes have afflicted the New England Clean Energy Connect line

insights.claim: The New York Independent System Operator did not assume CHPE would be available this summer, which its spokesperson credits as one reason the grid performed reliably during the July heat wave.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: The grid was insulated because nothing was counting on the asset — meaning CHPE's downtime is an investor problem now and a reliability problem only once planners start leaning on it.
insights.quote: A core principle of reliability planning is not relying on any single project.
insights.locator: The good news for New York is that the grid wasn't relying on CHPE yet

insights.claim: The path to CHPE mattering runs through utilities gaining confidence after the equipment is stress-tested over future years, creating a lag between an asset being energised and it being credited in reliability planning.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Capacity-value recognition lags physical completion by years — a timing mismatch that hits merchant transmission cash flows before it hits ratepayers.
insights.locator: The idea is that eventually, states and regions will be able to rely

insights.claim: Quebec has had intense drought for the past three years, eating into the water reserves used to generate electricity, so abundant hydropower may not always be available to ship south even when the transmission lines work.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Hydrology, not just wires, is the second-order risk to the Northeast import thesis — reservoir levels in Quebec are the leading indicator to track.
insights.locator: One thing to keep an eye on moving forward is the condition of Quebec's hydropower fleet
